0.why: TrigSeq.cpp takes this jack as a rising edge at 1V in Clock mode, and in Cv mode clamps getVoltage() to 0-10V and divides it across the set length

1.why: TrigSeq.cpp compares this jack against 1V, or against -1V when Reverse Input Voltage is set to Negative, at the moment a clock edge arrives

2.why: TrigSeq.cpp compares this jack against 1V as a level, or takes a rising edge when Run Input is set to Trig

3.why: TrigSeq.cpp takes this jack as a rising edge at 1V to jump to the reset step

4.why: TrigSeq.cpp adds this jack's voltage to the STEPS knob, 0-10V covering all sixteen steps

comment: The output has no family because TURING MODE changes what it carries: a trigger, gate or clock-width pulse normally, and a stepped control voltage in that mode. The RST knob is configured over 0 to 1 with a custom quantity (TrigSeq.cpp:161) rather than 1 to 16, because the same knob doubles as the TURING output attenuator; the original 1-to-16 line is commented out above it at :160. REV and RST are read only in clock mode.
